restrictions: Two-block ordinary collisions M0||M1, M0||M1' of 128 bytes on the complete padded sha256-r31 target from the standard IV; the difference is confined to W5..W9 of the second block (Li-Liu-Wang 2024 Table 6, restated in proof.md section 3).

One fixed public starting point (proof.md section 4); a 2560-entry pair table keyed by A(-1); four W5 difference classes; B = 2^48 first blocks M0(i) = BE_32(i)||BE_32(r) with one fresh uniform word r; caps of 4096 full matches and 2^34 bitmap hits, bounded by Markov's inequality.
Every returned pair is verified by recomputing both complete hashes; heuristics affect only success probability and cost.
Pricing: collision-frontier-v5, one selected compression = 1, other word operations 1/2140, with two operations charged per executed instruction (primitive plus fetch).

The time bound includes a declared 2^45-unit charge for the historical computation that produced the public characteristic and starting point (H-HISTORICAL-COST), supported by the authors' reported 76.8 thread-hours and a timed re-run of their public characteristic-search models.
Exploratory heuristic estimate; not a full-scale execution and not a rigorous proof of the success probability.

heuristics.statement: For distinct first blocks M0(i), the chaining words (h0, h1, h2) = (A-1, A-2, A-3) of f(IV, M0(i)) have the probabilities of independent uniform words for the table-entry match events and their same-key intersections (2^-45.678 full matches per block, exact overlap 0.000233 * 2^-48), and blocks are independent; with H-STEP3 this gives per-block success probability at least 2^-48 * 0.5247. The caps use only the marginals (Markov).
heuristics.scope: The 31-round compression from the standard IV on 2^48 counter-indexed first blocks; events defined by 32-bit equalities and set memberships on the output words.
heuristics.extrapolation: Standard modelling assumption of two-block attacks. Tested at reduced scale on the attack's exact counter-indexed block family: organizer experiment match-word-uniformity (single events h0, h1, h2 against the structured key, V6 and row-5 sets); author C run over 2^32 blocks of single, pairwise and triple joint events down to probability 2^-25.25 (all |z| < 0.9); and Step 3 on free words of real blocks conditioned on the real h1 match event (0.1143 vs 0.1202 unconditioned, z = -0.83). The full 2^-46 event is extrapolated.
heuristics.limitations: The full-match event (about 2^-46 per block) and dependence at that scale are not observed; the reduced-scale tests cover single-word events and joint events to 2^-25.25 only.

heuristics.statement: Given a full match, Step 3 of proof.md section 5.4 (with its caps) succeeds with entry-weighted average probability at least pbar = 0.1050 over the four equally likely W5 classes.
heuristics.scope: Step 3 on matched states from the fixed starting point, with uniformly distributed free chaining words A-4, E-4..E-1.
heuristics.extrapolation: Author Monte Carlo (10^6 uniform-C samples per class; 99% lower bounds average 0.1102), 12,000 simulated matches, and Step 3 on states with real free chaining words (real-state-completion: author run 438/4096 = 0.1069 with uniform entry weights; previous organizer run 29/256 with W8 weights); fresh-completions 256/256 on one real matched state.
heuristics.limitations: States with real (h0, h1, h2) at an actual match are not sampled (about 2^46 work); pbar = 0.1050 lies about 0.8 standard errors below the author's 4096-trial measurement.

heuristics.statement: The total historical computation that produced the public 31-step characteristic (Table 6) and the starting point is at most 2^45 target-compression units under collision-frontier-v5 pricing.
heuristics.scope: SAT/SMT characteristic search, starting-point solving, and the practical search that produced the published pair from which the starting point is read.
heuristics.extrapolation: Starting point: the authors report 76.8 thread-hours for the practical search that produced the published pair. Characteristic: the authors' public models find_dc_model_31_256.py and correct_dc_model_31_256.py were re-run to termination on one core (stage 1: 4148 s, minimum weight 21 proved; stage 2: 548 s; 1.30 core-hours in total, peak 1.6 GB); 100 times that is charged for design iterations. Conversion: one core-hour <= 2^35.97 units. Total 2^43.64 <= 2^45 charged.
heuristics.limitations: The authors' own characteristic-search computation and its memory are not reported; the bound relies on the timed re-run of their public tool, a 100x allowance, a generous cycle-to-operation conversion (5 GHz, 8 word operations per cycle), and an assumed 64 GiB memory for their SAT runs. Sensitivity: a 2^47 charge would give time_log2 about 48.6.
